title: Config Canary Harmonizer with Cohort Probing and SLO Fencing
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a canary orchestration component that composes batching/caching config proposals and applies them to traffic cohorts with automated SLO fencing and anomaly-driven rollback. The harmonizer will run recommendation plans from the optimizer, probe cohorts in controlled windows, and gate full rollout based on SLO signals (latency/throughput/error rates).
background: We have multiple optimization flows producing batching and KV-cache proposals. Past rollouts have seen silent regressions when small latency spikes propagate to tail latency and downstream services. Current canaries run simple traffic splits without cohort-aware probing or layered fences. We need a coordinator that composes safe canary plans: staged traffic ramps, diversity of cohorts (size/seq-length/hardware), and SLO fencing that automatically isolates, throttles, or reverts configs when anomalies are detected.
goal: Reduce per-token serving cost by enabling safe automated apply of batching/caching recommendations while ensuring no significant regressions to latency or throughput SLOs. Provide an auditable canary lifecycle and clear observability for rollouts.
success_metrics: p95 latency change <= +5% for production cohorts
canary success rate >= 95% (no manual rollback) over 30 days
detected anomalies trigger rollback within 2 minutes on average
acceptance_criteria: H1: Harmonizer can accept an optimizer plan (batch_size, prefetch_profile, kv_cache_policy) and create a canary definition
H2: System can assign >=4 distinct cohorts automatically (short/med/long seqs, bursty vs steady)
H3: Canary ramps traffic 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% with configurable hold windows
H4: SLO fence evaluates latency/throughput/error KPIs with configurable thresholds and aborts rollout if violated
H5: Canary lifecycle is auditable: event stream to console, links to PR and recommendation, and post-canary report generated
H6: Integration tests simulate anomaly injection and verify automated rollback within defined SLA
implementation_steps: 1) Define canary plan schema and storage (immutable canary objects referencing optimizer proposals)
2) Build cohort-selection service that samples routing keys across seq-length and customer cohorts (approximation by token length histogram)
3) Implement canary runner: staged traffic shifts, hold windows, metric sampling, and gating API
4) Extend SLO evaluator: streaming rule engine supporting composite rules (latency + throughput + error) and anomaly detectors (z-score and EWMA baselines)
5) Integrate with config applier: safe-apply API that supports staged apply and immediate revert
6) Add observability: per-cohort dashboards, diffed token cost metrics, and canary runbook notes
7) E2E tests and chaos scenarios: simulate slow kernels, transient infra noise, and burst traffic; verify fences and rollback
rollback_plan: If SLO fence triggers: immediately freeze and rollback canary cohort to baseline config using safe-apply revert API
Notify on-call via PagerDuty with prefilled incident template (include canary_id, cohort, recent metric deltas, PR link)
If rollback fails: escalate to runtime-sre and initiate emergency traffic diversion to fallback model variant (lower-capacity but lower-latency) and open postmortem
Post-rollback: auto-create follow-up task to run root-cause probe job capturing KV cache hits, batching windows, and kernel queue lengths
monitoring_and_alerts: Create canary KPI dashboard: per-cohort p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model queue depth, kv_cache_hit_rate, cost_per_token
Prometheus alerts: canary_latency_p95_increase > 5% for 3 samples => page SRE
Anomaly detector alert: z-score > 4 on latency or throughput => automated pause + notify
Audit logs: every config apply/rollback must record actor, plan hash, time, and metrics snapshot
testing_plan: Unit tests for canary plan validation and safety checks
Integration tests: staged ramp simulation with synthetic traffic generator across cohort types
Chaos tests: slow GPU kernel injection and KV-store flaps to confirm rollback triggers
Load test: run 1M requests through canary runner in staging with production-like distributions
